Raoul Pal Warns of Economic Singularity
On Saturday, in a post on
X
, Pal warned that the world was approaching a period of unprecedented economic disruption, driven by accelerating technological advances and persistent pressure on household finances.
"Your wages haven’t kept up with the cost of living for years now," Pal wrote, arguing that currency debasement was eroding people’s purchasing power.
"That’s the Everything Code," he added, referring to his broader economic thesis about the relationship between government financing, currency debasement and declining purchasing power.
Pal said the coming years could bring changes unlike anything people had experienced before.
"What is new is that we have maybe four years before the world as we know it stops working the way it does now," he wrote.
AI, Robotics and Crypto Could Reshape Global Economy
He pointed to AI, robotics, energy and cryptocurrency as technologies advancing so quickly that existing political and economic systems could struggle to adapt.
"The exponential technologies… are moving so fast that the systems built for the old world can’t keep up," Pal said.
He also warned that political divisions could deepen, trust in information could deteriorate and traditional business models could undergo fundamental changes.
Pal described the transformation as the "Economic Singularity," adding, "The window to get ahead of it all is closing."
The next four years are going to feel very different to anything we've lived through.
